rewind.transcript: So this morning I woke up at six thirty because the neighbour's dog was barking. I made a pour-over coffee, the kind with the paper filter, and drank it on the balcony while it was still a bit dark and cold. Then I showered, read the news on my phone for way too long, and walked my dog around the block. The grass was wet and he kept stopping to sniff every single tree. After that I answered a few emails and got dressed. That's pretty much what I remember.
Today was a normal day. I got up, went to class, had lunch, did some homework, ate dinner and then I went to sleep. Nothing really happened.

I woke up before my alarm, around five fifty, and the room was still blue. I made oatmeal with too much cinnamon and burned my tongue on the first spoonful. On the train in, a guy across from me was asleep holding a full cup of coffee and I spent the whole ride waiting for it to spill. It didn't. At work the morning was mostly a long planning meeting where nobody agreed on anything. For lunch I went to the taco truck on Fifth Street with Priya, and we sat on the steps outside the library because it was finally warm. In the afternoon I fixed a bug I'd been stuck on for two days, and I actually said yes out loud at my desk when the test passed. I left at six, picked up groceries, and cooked a stir fry while my sister called me about her wedding plans. We talked for an hour. I finished the night reading on the couch with the window open, listening to the rain start.

I didn't do much until about two in the afternoon, honestly. Then I went to the gym and did legs, which I regret now because I can barely walk up the stairs. After the gym I stopped at my mom's house and she made me take home a giant container of rice and beans. In the evening I watched the football game with my roommate. We ordered wings, our team lost in the last minute, and he threw a pillow at the TV.

mark_up.text: We didn't miss the deadline because we were lazy. We missed it because we said yes to everything.
Do you want the good news first, or the bad news? The good news is that sales are up, costs are down, and the team is growing.
Ten years ago, Sam asked me to help him move a couch. I said one hour, tops. We are still friends, and the couch is still stuck in the stairwell.
